text: Writing clean code is a skill that makes life easier for everyone who reads or works with your program. The main goal is readability—code should be as clear as plain English, so others can understand it quickly without long explanations. One important habit is following naming conventions: variable names should describe what they hold, like `userAge` instead of `x`, and functions should be named by their action, such as `calculateTotal()`. Instead of writing one long, complicated block, break the work into small, focused functions that each do one task. This practice greatly improves maintainability, because when you need to fix a bug or change a feature, you can find and update the right part in seconds, without breaking the rest of the system.
